string without context, so translations drifted (three words for seat,
commander damage in two forms) and missed official terms (Monarch left
in English, Korean prize cards using the Japanese word). Garbage like a
bare "x" passed validation. Since Oct 16 every run got a 401 because
agent shells point ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL at a proxy, so agents translated
by hand.

Add headless simulation core loop: Producer -> Receiver earns Money

A deterministic, fixed-timestep simulation (ADR-0001) that owns game state.
Commands (connect, disconnect) return success or a reasoned rejection;
size-1 Batches travel along Connections and the Receiver scores them
against its single Run, paying base x Run length. Randomness comes from a
seeded generator in game state and all balance numbers live in one
tuning config.

Disconnecting returns in-transit Batches to the Producer's queue, which
re-emits them first on reconnection, so Items are never dropped.

Save states: lift pause around a capture or restore

Pause suspends every guest thread through its suspend count, and those
counts are part of the state a capture records. A state saved while
paused therefore loaded with the game frozen, and loading while paused
left the later resume releasing threads the game had suspended itself.

Saving and loading now resume the title first and pause it again
afterwards, so states never record the pause and the user stays paused.

XeFG/XeLL: hand the game OptiScaler's copy, keep proxied modules loaded

A game loading its own libxess_fg.dll or libxell.dll while OptiScaler
has a copy loaded ends with two copies: OptiScaler's XeLL hooks never
see the game's calls and XeFG may pair with either XeLL. The game now
gets OptiScaler's copy, unless the file it asked for has a newer file
version (an XeFG update that came with the game stays the game's), and
a copy the game had loaded before OptiScaler is left to the loader.
Each case is logged with the versions.

Engine: end a game on its own thread (End table could deadlock)

GameSession.end() called game.setGameOver on the control socket's
thread: it takes Game's monitor and fires an event while the game
thread may be inside onEvent (the event bus's per-subscriber lock)
waiting for that monitor. A deadlock that would freeze the control
socket and so every table; StartingPlayerTest hit it in the full
suite. end() now sets a flag and marks the humans absent; the game
thread sets the game over at its next event. The test asserts the
game thread finishes after end().

Link's network client but left it in the game's map: the director waited

goes back to the main menu as the game's own Quit does, when a game's map
is loaded; the director looks for games again once the menu is up.

feat(android): Levik Game for the Direct build

Selected games only go through the VPN. Their UDP over IPv4 reaches the
nearest game exit through the levik-game helper, which sends two copies
along two paths, re-routes through the mesh and hands the relay token
over. Each game node link reaches only that node's relay through its own
SOCKS inbound. DNS, QUIC, TCP and IPv6 stay direct. Game node links never
become ordinary servers, including on Play.

home screen shows the live Game status.

is an http_done event delivered between two ticks (plugins::poll), to that

the window loses focus. So the ranked time is now measured on the server, from
two stamps: a signed start token handed out when a fresh daily begins

penalty is worked out by the server from how the chain was solved, not taken
from the game. The game's own clock is ignored for ranking.
